default.reference CUDA scan: its stock length dispatch clip(nextpow2(L), 128, 2048), timed in the same (runtime-chunk) binary and session as the other chunks
default.Triton Mamba-1 scan (ours): no library default exists; use the free length rule clip(nextpow2(L), 32, 1024), the stock dispatch of the reference scan transplanted to this kernel's chunk range, as 'default'; keep chunk 256 as a secondary row labelled 'borrowed SSD default'

proposal.best_static: one chunk per data set (and, as a separate row, one chunk per batch size), chosen as the chunk with the lowest total latency (the deployment objective; equivalently the lowest latency-weighted share) on the training prompt folds and scored on the held-out fold; report its per-call and latency-weighted regret. Every table that uses another criterion (per-call regret) or an in-sample choice labels it.
rationale: total latency is what a deployed static chunk minimizes, and the headline convention of the paper is the latency-weighted share
held out removes the in-sample/held-out label problem of Table 5
the same rule applies unchanged to every kernel and every timing convention
a kernel without a library default gets a zero-cost, untuned rule that an engineer would write, not a borrowed constant
